items.text: People show a tendency. <break time="0.8s" /> To trust ideas that correspond to their beliefs. <break time="0.8s" /> Even though there is little or no objective evidence to support them. <break time="0.8s" /> Such ideas may eventually turn out to be false. <break time="0.8s" /> If the assumptions underlying them. <break time="0.8s" /> Largely rely on subjective observations. <break time="0.8s" /> Careful thinkers thus try to test their existing beliefs. <break time="0.8s" /> Rather than simply maintaining them. <break time="0.8s" /> When new evidence does not support the idea that they have entertained. <break time="0.8s" /> They reexamine it. <break time="0.8s" /> From alternative viewpoints. <break time="0.8s" /> This inspires them. <break time="0.8s" /> To go about challenging the problematic belief. <break time="0.8s" /> Therefore, thinking reflectively about the existing beliefs. <break time="0.8s" /> Helps people adjust them. <break time="0.8s" /> According to available evidence. <break time="0.8s" /> Furthermore, it enables people to become less likely to accept new ideas. <break time="0.8s" /> Just because they are tempting. <break time="0.8s" /> Or consistent with what they have long believed. <break time="0.8s" /> Although individuals differ considerably in their belief systems. <break time="0.8s" /> Those who objectify and test their own beliefs. <break time="0.8s" /> Tend to think more critically. <break time="0.8s" /> Than those who do not.
